study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Elad et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Improving the predictive potential of diffusion MRI in schizophrenia using normative models -Towards subject-level classification

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Harmonized multi-site diffusion MRI dataset collated from 13 sites across separate studies (Cetin-Karayumak et al., 2020).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "dMRI data were collated from 13 different sites across a number of separate studies."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Elad2021.pdf.md: 2.1 | Participants, imaging acquisition, image preprocessing and harmonization procedures

answer.MULTI-SITE (N>=2): Normative model built from healthy controls; schizophrenia group used for evaluation/classification against controls.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy controls define the normative range and provide z-scores; schizophrenia group provides comparisons and classification targets.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we leveraged a large harmonized diffusion MRI dataset from 512 healthy controls and 601 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia, to study whether normative modeling can improve subject-level predictions from a binary classifier." ... "The normative model represents the distribution of the normative range within each ROI in the healthy controls"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Elad2021.pdf.md: Abstract; Elad2021.pdf.md: 2.3 | Construction of a normative model

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Healthy controls used to define the normative model; training-specific counts for the normative model are not explicitly reported.
